instruction: Choose a suitable finite-element simulation tool available in the current Windows fused environment. Use a command-line or scripting workflow. Use the selected finite-element simulation tool to perform a torsion analysis of a circular shaft (Variant B). Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. 1. Part: 3D Deformable Solid, Revolution - Sketch in the X-Y plane: draw a rectangle from (0,0) to (6,72) - The left vertical edge at X=0 is the revolution axis (global Y-axis) - Revolve 360 deg to create a solid cylinder with diameter 12 mm and length 72 mm, aligned with the global Y-axis 2. Property: - Material Steel: E = 210000 MPa, nu = 0.3 - Solid Homogeneous section 3. Assembly: Create an instance. 4. Step: Static, General, named Step-Torque-B. 5. Interaction: - Create a Reference Point (RP-1) at the center of the free end face (Y=72 mm, X=0, Z=0) - Use Constraint > Coupling to kinematically couple the free end face and RP-1 (all 6 DOFs) - Apply Encastre to the fixed end face (Y=0) 6. Load: - Apply a torque (Moment) = 920 N*mm at RP-1 about the shaft axis (global Y-axis, i.e., component MY) 7. Mesh: - Global seed size: 4 mm - Element type: appropriate three-dimensional solid element formulation 8. Job: Create Job-Torsion-B and submit for solving. 9. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop, and write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json` with numeric fields for the requested metrics.
